column1: # San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo. Baptisms, folio 470, ACT No. 1720.
# Margin: "Vide Duplicado fol. 112 num 16". Priest: Martin Perez.
# Image read 13 September 2026 by the DeepZoom tile method, level 12 (11 x 8 tiles).
# The index for this act was made BY A COMPUTER - FamilySearch says so on the record - and it
# garbled the parents into "Julia Juanico, Luis Lorena" with BOTH marked Mother. The image
# settles it, and gives four grandparents the index never surfaced.

column3: Folio 470 of the opening; act 1721 (Jose Maria Luis, 7 July) follows.

column2: 6 July 1886, "En seis de Julio de mil ocho cientos ochenta y seis"
*** CANDIDO JAIME *** - the margin heading reads "Candido Jaime Lerena"
column3: *** A SEVENTH CHILD of Luis Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico, and the archive had five. *** Named for his maternal grandfather Candido and his godfather Jaime.

column2: 13 September 1884, "que nacio el trece de Setiembre de mil ocho cientos ochenta y cuatro"
column3: Baptised at 21 months, not as an infant - the same late-baptism habit that may explain why Pablo Armando is not in the Rosario register as a newborn.

column2: hijo legitimo de Don Luis Lerena Lenguas y de Dona Julia Juanico, ORIENTALES
column3: Both stated Uruguayan in their own parish, twenty-two years after the 1864 marriage act.

column2: abuelos paternos: Don Luis y Dona Justiniana Lenguas
column3: Confirms from the image what the compound surname implies: Luis Lerena married a Lenguas, and their son carried both.

column2: *** "maternos: Don Candido y Dona Juliana Gonzalez" ***
column3: *** CLOSES AN OPEN QUESTION. *** Candido Juanico's wife was JULIANA GONZALEZ - asked by this archive as an open question and answered here by a document, not an index.

column2: fueron padrinos: Don Jaime Herrera y Dona Maria Lerena
column3: *** The godmother is the baby's own eldest sister *** - Maria Julia Margarita, b. Rosario 1865 - and the godfather is the man she married in the SAME PARISH four months later, 3 November 1886. They stood together at the font while betrothed.
